# Testing group-ring matrices with characters of a subgroup generated by support products

## Statement

Let \(F=(f_{ij})\) be a finite matrix over the complex group ring of a discrete group \(G\).
Form a bipartite graph with a row vertex \(i\), a column vertex \(j\), and one edge from \(i\) to \(j\) for each group element in the support of \(f_{ij}\), labeled by that element.
Read inverse labels on reversed edges and multiply labels in path order.
On a connected component fix a row root and let \(H\le G\) be the group of label products of closed paths at that root.
Choose a spanning tree, and write \(p_v\) for the product on its path from the root to \(v\).
The row and column operations
\[
                 f_{ij}\longmapsto f'_{ij}=p_i f_{ij}p_j^{-1}
\]
put all entries in \(\mathbb CH\) and preserve their matrix rank.
This is a minimal subgroup for this operation up to conjugation: if row and column group units put all the entries of that component in \(\mathbb CL\), a conjugate of \(H\) lies in \(L\).
One may apply the construction just to a selected square submatrix.

For an integer character \(\psi:H\to\mathbb Z\), put \(w_{ij}=\min\psi(\operatorname{supp}f'_{ij})\) on the nonempty entries.
Suppose a selected square matrix on \(q\) rows and columns has a unique perfect matching minimizing the sum of these weights.
If the lowest-weight part of each matched entry has full scalar regular rank, that square matrix has regular rank \(q\).
In particular, distinct monomial minima on the matched entries suffice, with no scalar injectivity hypothesis.
Here a monomial minimum means just one group element realizes the minimum within that entry.
Regular scalar injectivity on \(H\) also suffices, and it is enough that it hold on \(\ker\psi\).
The character need not extend to \(G\).

As a consequence, take any two-by-two corner with four nonzero entries in an actual regular rank-one matrix over a group satisfying scalar injectivity.
After the above operations on the corner, let \(\mathcal P_{ij}\) denote the convex hull of the images of \(\operatorname{supp}f'_{ij}\) in \(H_{\rm ab}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb R\).
Then its Newton polytopes satisfy the Minkowski sum identity
\[
          \mathcal P_{11}+\mathcal P_{22}
                     =\mathcal P_{12}+\mathcal P_{21}.
\]
It applies to each corner of the order-26 [rank-one remainder](Yin_C_A0199_v1.md#syzygies-and-the-single-denominator) even when its ambient group has finite abelianization.
A strict inequality in one direction excludes the proposed remainder.

## Localization and the weighted matching

For an edge \(i\to j\) of label \(g\), the transformed label \(p_i g p_j^{-1}\) is the word on a closed path based at the root.
For a tree edge it is the identity.
Conversely these transformed labels and their inverses generate all closed products by cancellation of consecutive vertex factors.
For any other placement of all edge labels into \(L\) by row and column units, write the edge transformations as \(q_i g q_j^{-1}\).
A closed product then belongs to \(L\) after conjugation by the same root factor, proving minimality.
Right-coset replication computes the regular rank over \(H\) or \(G\) with the same result.

Reorder columns so the unique minimizing matching is the diagonal.
For every off-diagonal nonempty position give the directed edge \(i\to j\) cost \(w_{ij}-w_{ii}\).
Every simple directed cycle has strictly positive total cost, since changing the diagonal matching along that cycle gives a different matching.
Subtract a sufficiently small positive rational \(\epsilon\) from each edge cost so that all directed cycles still have nonnegative cost.
There are finitely many simple cycles; when there are none, any positive \(\epsilon\) works.
Add a source joined to all vertices by zero-cost edges.
Shortest path costs \(u_i\) from it are finite rational numbers and obey
\[
                     u_j-u_i\le w_{ij}-w_{ii}-\epsilon
\]
on each off-diagonal edge.

In \(f'_{ij}\) multiply each group label \(g\) by \(z^{\psi(g)}\) with \(z\ne0\).
For a positive real parameter use the row factor \(z^{-w_{ii}+u_i}\) and column factor \(z^{-u_j}\).
For positive real \(z\) the diagonal minimum becomes zero and every off-diagonal minimum is at least \(\epsilon\).
The row and column scalings do not affect rank at a nonzero parameter.
The scaled matrix converges in norm as \(z\downarrow0\) to the diagonal of the matched lowest-weight parts.
If these scalars are injective, spectral cutoffs of the diagonal give limiting inferior rank \(q\).
The original Laurent polynomial matrix has maximum rank at generic points of the unit circle by [finite polynomial evaluation](Yin_C_A0022_v1.md#simultaneous-generic-rank-and-degeneration).
All its circle ranks equal the original one by genuine character twists of \(H\); hence it has full rank.
A lowest-weight part supported at height \(j\) can be multiplied by a single inverse group translation of that same height to put it in \(\mathbb C\ker\psi\).
This proves the stated sufficient hypotheses, including monomials.

## A necessary support identity for a fractional-rank witness

For the two-by-two application, all integral linear functionals on \(H_{\rm ab}\) are characters of the very subgroup containing the transformed entries.
If the two sums of their support minima differed for one such functional, one of the two perfect matchings would win uniquely.
The previous argument would give regular rank two for the corner, impossible inside a rank-one matrix.
The group \(H\) is finitely generated by the finitely many transformed labels.
Rational functionals on the finite-dimensional real abelianization are dense and can be scaled to integral functionals of its free lattice.
Continuity of the minimum of a linear functional on each compact polytope gives equality for every real functional.
The minimum on a Minkowski sum is the sum of minima, and a compact convex polytope is determined by all these minima.
This yields the asserted support identity.
A corner whose resulting subgroup has finite abelianization passes this test automatically; in that case the support identity gives no rank decision.
